claims: Cameron Boozer and Cayden Boozer are fraternal twins.
Cameron Boozer and Cayden Boozer play basketball for Duke during the 2025-26 season.
Cameron Boozer and Cayden Boozer committed as 2025 five-star recruits.
Cameron Boozer and Cayden Boozer are from Columbus High School in Miami.
Cameron Boozer and Cayden Boozer are sons of Carlos Boozer.
Cameron Boozer is a 6'9" forward.
Cayden Boozer is a 6'4" guard.
Cameron Boozer is ACC Player of the Year.
Duke won the 2026 ACC Tournament Championship.
Cameron Boozer earned MVP honors.
Cameron Boozer leads Duke in points with 22.5 as of March 2026.
Cameron Boozer leads Duke in rebounds with 10.2 as of March 2026.
Cameron Boozer leads Duke in assists with 4.2 as of March 2026.
Cayden Boozer stepped into a starting role during the 2026 ACC tournament.
Cayden Boozer stepped into a starting role following an injury to teammate Caleb Foster.
Cameron Boozer and Cayden Boozer are sons of CeCe Boozer.
Carlos Boozer is a former NBA All-Star.
Carlos Boozer won the 2001 NCAA title at Duke.
Cameron Boozer and Cayden Boozer have an older brother named Carmani.
Carmani had sickle cell anemia.
The twins were born to help cure their older brother Carmani.
Stem cells from the birth of Cameron Boozer and Cayden Boozer were used for a successful life-saving transplant.
Cameron Boozer and Cayden Boozer chose Duke over Miami and Florida in October 2024.
